catalog_locator: Introduction, §4 'Lexical tone in Shua', pp. vii–viii (PDF pp. 9–10); saved file the copy we hold and its(layer (src -> shua1254)
catalog_quote: Tone in Shua has not been systematically studied. Hence, the patterns provided in the following are preliminary and may be subject to change, once a more dedicated study is undertaken. Shua distinguishes three tone levels H(igh), M(id) and L(ow), which may be combined into two level (HH, MM) and four contour melodies (MH, HM, ML, HL). Like in related Kalahari Khoe languages (see Fehn 2016 on Ts’ixa, 2019 on Khwe), the tone-bearing unit in Shua is the mora, rather than the syllable. Inherited lexical roots consistently display two morae, while grammatical elements may be monomoraic. Elderkin (2004) reconstructs four basic tonal melodies for proto-Khoe (*HH, *HL, *LH, *LL), which may undergo depression in the presence of voiced or aspirated onsets. Depressed patterns are also found in roots with “narrowing”, i.e., roots which may have displayed a still unknown onset or phonation type in t…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Shua is a lexical tone language (H/M/L on a bimoraic root, six melodies); the only modern first-hand description says nothing about word stress at all. The one explicit stress remark located (Vossen 1997, snippet) is family-level: whether stress ('Druckakzent') has distinctive function in Khoe languages is 'still largely unresolved', and his concrete stress observations concern ǁAni and ǂHaba, not Shua.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned for Shua (Vossen 1997's primary/secondary stress remark on >2-syllable verbs is about ǁAni/ǂHaba).
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Tone: depressor effects of voiced/aspirated onsets and 'narrowed' roots shift the default reflexes of proto-Khoe *HH/*HL/*LH/*LL (Table 6, p. viii).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical roots (citation forms) in a draft dictionary; tone marking flagged as tentative. Dictionary covers Western Shua, Eastern Shua and Deti (2024 fieldwork).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog shua1254 'Shua' is a dialect cluster (Western Shua = Danisi; Eastern/Nata Shua incl. Cara and ǀXaise; Deti). Vossen 1997/2013 also counted Ts'ixa as a Shua dialect, but Glottolog and Fehn (2023) treat it as a separate language (tsix1234); the Fehn 2016 grammar and 2024 dictionary held by the project are Ts'ixa, not Shua. The quoted tone statement (Fehn, Leepang & Rocha 2025) covers Western Shua, Eastern Shua and Deti jointly; Vossen 2013's tone remarks are specifically on Cara and Deti.

sources.note: Nothing about stress. Describes lexical tone: three levels H/M/L, level melodies HH, MM and contours MH, HM, ML, HL; tone-bearing unit is the mora; roots bimoraic. Tone 'not been systematically studied'; patterns preliminary. Covers Western Shua, Eastern Shua and Deti (fieldwork 2024).
